title: NCBI Bacterial Pathogen Data Curation Protocol for GenomeTrakr Submissions
author: Tina Pfefer
materials: How to make edits to BioProject records:
Query for SRR accession you'd like to update:

steps.title: Edit BioProject Information
steps.instruction: Update the Title, Organism, Description, URL, or publications for a BioProject via the submission portal.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Manage Data' tab in the submission portal or go to https://dataview.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
Select the 'BioProject (##)' tab from the menu to view the list of group bioprojects
Click on the specific BioProject that requires editing
Enter the updated information in the available edit/add fields
Click 'next' and 'submit'
Wait for the confirmation prompt indicating updates are in progress

steps.title: Request BioProject Assistance
steps.instruction: Contact NCBI for BioProject errors, processing issues, or conversion/re-assignment of BioProjects.

substeps.instruction: For Pathogen Detection submissions: Email pd-help@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov with the BioProject accession in the subject line
For all other (non-Pathogen Detection) submissions: Email bioprojecthelp@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov with the BioProject accession in the subject line

steps.title: Update or Correct PD BioSample Records
steps.instruction: Submit requests to update, correct, or add fields/attributes to PD BioSample records, including retractions and linkage changes, via email to pd-help@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.

substeps.instruction: Include the lab name and request date in the subject line (e.g., 'FDA BioSample update, Dec 10, 2019')
For metadata updates: Attach a tab-delimited text file with BioSample accessions in the first column and the fields to be updated to the right
For BioSample retractions: List the specific SAMN######## accessions and the reason for retraction in the email body
For BioProject re-assignment: Specify the new BioProject accession(s) in a column in the attached file; if SRA or GenBank data is associated, explicitly request their reassignment as well
Ensure organism names include binomial name (Genus species), subspecies (if present), and serovar/serotype information
For Salmonella enterica: Enter serotyping information in the 'serovar' field, not the 'serotype' field

Avoid using prohibited terms in strain/isolate fields: 'bacteria sp.', 'strain', 'environmental', 'soil', 'clinical isolate', 'NA', 'whole organism', 'Microbial', or any general taxonomic information (genus/species names)

steps.title: Update SRA Metadata via Portal
steps.instruction: Edit sequence metadata (library ID, strategy, platform, instrument), associated accessions, or release dates using the submission portal.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Manage Data' tab or navigate to https://dataview.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
Query for the SRR accession to be updated
Click on the BioProject accession link
Scroll to the SRA records list, select the desired records via checkboxes, and click 'Edit metadata'
Modify the metadata (e.g., enter a correct BioSample accession to resolve a sample-swap); changed fields will turn yellow
Click 'Submit'

steps.title: Retract SRA Records
steps.instruction: Request retraction of SRA records due to poor quality data, unresolvable sample mix-ups, or multiple runs per isolate by emailing pd-help@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.

substeps.instruction: Include a list of SRR accessions to retract and the specific reason for retraction
Use a subject line such as 'FDA SRA retractions, Dec 10, 2019'
Note: Do not attempt to re-submit the same files after retraction, as they will be flagged as duplicates

steps.title: Move SRA Data Between BioProjects
steps.instruction: If the submission portal does not allow moving SRA data from one BioProject to another, request the move via email.

substeps.instruction: Send the move request to pd-help@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov to ensure all linked records (e.g., GenBank) are handled
